newsitem.title: UK: Germany in charm offensive to free EU telecoms.
newsitem.headline: Germany in charm offensive to free EU telecoms.

text.p: German Post and Telecommunications Minister Wolfgang Boetsch said on Friday he would use "charm and pressure" to encourage European neighbours to make the necessary arrangements for liberalising their telecom markets by 1998.

Speaking in an interview on CNBC television, Boetsch said Germany would follow Britain and was on track for opening up its telecommunications networks to competition on January 1, 1998, along with France.
But he said he was "a little bit afraid" that other European countries were lagging. "We will use charm and pressure," he said. "I think we have to do both."
The European Union has agreed that most countries will open their telecoms markets to full competition by January 1, 1998.

The Commission has also outlined a series of initiatives, including streamlined procedures for taking legal action against recalcitrant governments and new rules for handling unfair competition complaints from telecoms operators.
Germany has estimated that the market volume of its telecoms industry alone will be larger than that for vehicles by 2000.
It has also predicted that the total world market available to German firms will be 1.5 trillion marks.
